summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all five paragraphs of the selected Latin working source. Both preserve the universal rescue obligation, the comparison with suffering in chains, self-inflicted death, guilt for another person’s blood, and the necessary action and exclusion warning. The notes disclose the unusual reflexive Latin wording and the bounded, damaged Greek alternative without replacing the continuous Latin or presenting a reconstructed Greek sentence as preserved text. Their disclosures are compatible with the supplied project reports. Acceptance concerns these supplied drafts and disclosures only; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify the cited editions, or establish exhaustive collation.
